\section*{Exploratory: feature sets without run lengths (deviation D13)}
\label{sec:supp-posthoc}

Not registered. The closed-set attack of question 4 on two feature sets without times that drop the lengths of runs: \texttt{letter\_runs\_unit}, in which every run of letter keys is one token whatever its length and every other press one token, and \texttt{all\_runs\_unit}, in which every run of presses of the same category is one token whatever its length; both keep the order. The predicted logs, the distance, the candidates and the tie-breaking of each trial, the values of K and the intervals are those of the registered attack, and every run reproduced the registered \texttt{no\_time} and \texttt{counts\_only} at every K before it wrote these values. \texttt{all\_runs\_unit} is derived from \texttt{letter\_runs\_unit}, so the accuracy of \texttt{letter\_runs\_unit} is the larger of the two; Raw is the accuracy of the set alone. The registered near-chance rule is applied as an exploratory judgement, from the two macOS cells, with the Windows judgement as its qualification; the registered judgement and recommendation do not change. --: no value.
